POPPY ROW

Fury as veteran barred entry from Wetherspoons pub for wearing poppy as he’s told remembrance symbol is ‘too political’

Benedict Elliot
Published: 11:46, 26 Oct 2026
|
Updated: 13:11, 26 Oct 2026
Add us as a preferred source
282 comments282
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 9:11
Instaread

A VETERAN has been left fuming after being barred entry from a Wetherspoons pub for wearing a poppy – with the remembrance symbol said to be “too political”.

Scott Schillemore, 33, was left gobsmacked after being told: “You’re not coming in” by a bouncer at The Star Wetherspoon in Gosport, Hampshire.

Advertisement

Shocking footage shows Wetherspoon bosses turning him away with one saying his remembrance symbol is “too political”.

The ex-Royal Artillery gunner was trying to visit the boozer for a pint with pals on Sunday afternoon when he was refused entry.

Dad-of-three Scott, from Portsmouth, Hampshire, told The Sun: “It was very abrupt.

“As we approached the entrance, the doorman pointed his finger at us and said: ‘You’re wearing a poppy, you’re not coming in’.

Cyclists ignore Khan’s ‘pedestrian-only’ rules for Oxford Street hours into ban

“I was in complete shock and disbelief.

“I lost a very good friend in Afghanistan.

Advertisement

“We yearly go into Wetherspoons on Remembrance Sunday to raise a glass to absent friends.

“But not anymore. There is no chance I’m ever going back to a Wetherspoons.”

Scott, who served in the Army from 2009 to 2015, added: “I’m now a door supervisor myself and have been doing it many years and I’ve never seen anything like it.

“If they were my instructions to follow I would have left the door and walked away immediately.”

He added: “Wetherspoons still sells poppies, but we’re not allowed to enter a pub with one?

Advertisement

“It’s ludicrous.”

The Royal British Legion states that the red poppy is neutral.

Wearing it raises funds for veterans, current service members, and their families through organisations like the Royal British Legion.

Advertisement

In the video the bouncer can be heard saying “he’s been giving his instructions” and can’t allow Scott and his two friends, who are also veterans, in.

He can be heard saying: “Put it in your pocket, take it off, you can (enter),” before adding: “Doors are closed.”

He adds: “I’m here to do a job.”

The pub’s manager then comes out and tells Scott and his pals: “It’s blanket. Anything that could be seen as political is a no.”

The protest in Gosport that day had nothing to do with the denial of entry, The Sun understands from the footage.

Advertisement

Locals wearing poppies including elderly women can also be seen being barred entry.

A Wetherspoon spokesperson said: “Wetherspoon has been a long- standing supporter of the Royal British Legion Poppy Appeal, with poppies for sale in our pubs, including the Star. There is no ban on poppies in Wetherspoon pubs.

“However there were some standard security measures in place today, as a result of demonstrations in the town.

“Unfortunately, some members of the public, including some wearing poppies, did not gain entry to the pub.

“The pub closed to all customers, on advice of the police, at 1700 and remains closed today.

Advertisement

“We apologise to any regular customers who have been inconvenienced by today’s events and look to forward to welcoming everyone back tomorrow.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Hampshire Constabulary spokesperson said: “Following the protest in Gosport a number of people gathered in Gosport High Street.

“No offences were identified and police did not ask any pubs to shut their doors. The group soon dispersed on their own.”
